slideDifferences.nativeText:
When we talk about  common life events we can use simple present and certain time phrases to state them in the future. Check the following examples.
TO CONSIDER

Use the simple present plus phrases in future to state them ahead in time. 
The phrases must reflect a close future. 
 Respect the simple present rules.
Simple Present + Future Phrase
I have a test this Tuesday.
Do you have a test this Tuesday?
They have to do laundry this weekend.
Do they have to do laundry this weekend?
He goes for his school performance tonight.
Does he go for his school performance tonight?

native.joinedText:
At home!


Don’t you have a test tomorrow? 
Yes, mum. I start studying in some minutes. 
Tommy it is 8 o’clock, very late!
Easy, mum! I finish reading this pages in some minutes 
       and I get to it.
If you don’t pass the test tomorrow, you will be grounded 
       until you are married.  
I am going to pass mum not to worry. Hey BTW, do we have a 
       family meeting tomorrow?
Yes! Tomorrow, your grandma is on her birthday. 
Oh…! I want to hang out with my friends tomorrow night... 
Sorry, we have a family commitment, you are coming with us!
Oh great! Another boring family meeting.
C. Read the following dialogue and state if the sentences are true (T) or false (F). After that, read the dialogue with your teacher.
1.  He does not have a test tomorrow.	 	(T) (F)
2. He starts studying in some minutes.	 	(T) (F)
3. It is 10 PM.					 	(T) (F)
4. He is reading.				 	(T) (F)
5.  He will be grounded until he is
married, if does not pass.			 	(T) (F)
6.  They have a family meeting tomorrow 
night.					 		 (T) (F)
7.  He is not hanging out with friends.	 	 (T) (F)
8. He is happy for attending the family
meeting.					 	 (T) (F)
